summary.oneLiner: Jasch Gauging Technologies is a single-product capital-goods maker of industrial gauges used for on-line measurement of thickness, grammage, moisture and coating weight in the paper, plastics, steel, galvanizing and non-ferrous rolling industries.
summary.business: The Company manufactures Industrial Gauges & Equipment only. These are used for on-line measurement of thickness, grammage, moisture and ash content in the paper-making industry, and for on-line measurement of thickness and coating weight in plastics, steel, sheet rolling, galvanizing, aluminium foil and non-ferrous metal rolling. The gauges are technology-based capital goods designed and manufactured on in-house developed technology, sold to Indian customers spread across the country and exported (earnings received in USD and EUR).

Industrial Gauges & Equipment: On-line thickness / grammage / moisture & ash measurement gauges (paper)
On-line thickness & coating-weight gauges (plastics, steel, sheet rolling, galvanizing, aluminium foil, non-ferrous rolling)

currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no expansion or capex project. There is a single manufacturing unit and management's stated plan is to maximize output from that existing unit rather than add capacity: 'The Company will focus on sustaining its growth momentum in the current year and will focus on maximizing the output from the unit.' The only capital-asset-related disclosures are negative: capital investment on energy conservation equipment was Nil, expenditure on Research and Development was Nil, no technology was imported in the last three years, and foreign-currency expenditure on 'Capital Goods & Component' was nil in both FY26 and FY25. The Company also confirms it had no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company at either the beginning or the end of the year, and no CSR capital assets were created or acquired during the year. On the energy side the Company operates 100 KVA of solar panels which produced about 80,000 units of electric energy in a year — captive power for the plant, not manufacturing capacity. A '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE — CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block (estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for) is present in the bundle but arrives with only the heading and column labels and carries no figure, so no capex quantum can be read off it.

risks.risk: User-industry concentration in a late-cycle capital-goods niche
risks.note: Industrial Gauges & Equipment are classified as capital goods bought by the paper, plastic, steel and galvanizing industries; revenues and profits depend on growth of those industries, and management notes that in a downward trend in the economy investment in capital goods is the last priority of an enterprise.
The Company has only manufactured Industrial Gauges & Equipment, with output coming from one unit — there is no second product line or site to absorb a demand or operational shock.

Management states that excessive exposure to a few large clients has the potential to adversely affect sales and profitability if clients fail or shift to other manufacturers; it argues customers are currently fairly spread across the country and efforts are underway to enlarge presence in global markets.

risks.risk: Global trade disruption and tariff wars
risks.note: The Directors' Report flags that ongoing global disturbances along with tariff wars across the globe may impact sales during FY2026-27 — material given the Company's export exposure (FOB export earnings in USD and EUR).

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation on a two-sided FX book
risks.note: The Industrial Gauges System has large export potential providing a natural hedge, but raw material is imported on a deferred-payment basis, leaving amounts payable in foreign exchange; transactions are on current-account basis with no other deferred FX liabilities.

Increases in bank interest rates hit profitability because the increase cannot always be passed on to customers; management relies on efficient inventory and working-capital management to contain interest cost.

risks.risk: Technological obsolescence in a technology-based product
risks.note: The product is a technology-based capital good; the Company relies on in-house developed technology that it says is continuously upgraded and therefore sees no near-term obsolescence threat, but R&D expenditure for the year was disclosed as Nil, so the upgrade effort is not visible as spend.

Management describes the cyber threat landscape as vast and continuously evolving and concedes that despite complex passwords, time-based OTPs and current anti-virus/anti-malware/security patching, criminals may still be one step ahead.

Management states the Company, its Directors, Promoters and Officers may get involved in legal and regulatory proceedings and any adverse decision may have a material adverse effect on business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations; no specific proceeding is disclosed in this material.
